problem: The formula NF = NFmin + (4Rn/Z0)·|Γs − Γopt|²/((1 − |Γs|²)|1 + Γopt|²) is the standard expression for the linear noise factor F, not for the noise figure in dB. The chapter uses NF in dB everywhere else (1.5 dB in the example, 12 dB gain, etc.), so a student who substitutes a dB value into this equation gets a wrong answer.
fix: Write it as F = Fmin + (4Rn/Z0)·|Γs − Γopt|²/((1 − |Γs|²)|1 + Γopt|²), define F as the linear noise factor, Fmin as its minimum value, and add NF(dB) = 10 log₁₀ F.

problem: The text calls ωT = gm/Cgs 'the transit frequency' without saying it is an angular frequency in rad/s. Students will confuse it with fT = gm/(2πCgs) quoted in datasheets, and then get Rin off by 2π.
fix: Say: ωT = gm/Cgs is the angular unity-current-gain (transit) frequency in rad/s; the datasheet value is fT = ωT/2π = gm/(2πCgs) in Hz.

problem: 'Pick Ls for 50 Ω and Lg for the channel' is unclear — 'the channel' has no defined meaning here.
fix: Say: choose Ls so that Rin = ωT Ls = 50 Ω, then choose Lg so that ω0 = 1/√((Lg + Ls)Cgs) equals the channel frequency.

problem: 'The cascode device adds little noise because the same bias current flows through both transistors' is loose. Equal current alone does not explain the small contribution; the cascode transistor's noise is small when referred to the input because it is divided by the gain of the common-source stage.
fix: Say: the cascode transistor carries the same current, and its own noise, referred to the input, is divided by the voltage gain of the common-source device, so it adds little to the overall noise figure.

problem: 'Cheap, integrates with CMOS' is circular: a MOSFET is CMOS.
fix: Say: 'Cheap; sits on the same CMOS die as the mixer and baseband'.

problem: 'Input-referred noise floor with NF = −104 dBm + 1.5 dB = −102.5 dBm' reads as if NF were an addition to a floor; the wording hides that the noise floor is being raised by the noise figure.
fix: Say: input-referred noise floor = thermal floor + NF = −104 dBm + 1.5 dB = −102.5 dBm.
